Olive oil has a low smoke point. Clarified butter, vegetable or canola oil might be a better choice.

Thaw out the amount you want to cook by placing in a zip lock bag and then place the bag in a bowl of room temp water. (Don't use hot water). Replace the water when it gets too cold. When the shrimp are thawed out, drain excess moisture and bring the shrimp up to room temperature (leave it about 20 mins or so covered).

Why? The key with shrimp is that they cook really quickly. (1-3 minutes in most cases.) You want to get the temperature up so that the insides cook as quickly as the outside. They'll turn pinkish in color and go from translucent when raw to opaque when cooked.

When cooking, if they shrink to half the size of what they were raw, you've definitely overcooked them.

If I'm making a pasta dish with spinach and shrimp, I'll cook everything else first and then add in the shrimp last, turn off the heat, and then mix that shit up. The temperature of the dish will cook the raw shrimp without overcooking.
